name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,611

clue.text: One found in bed happened to have a bad back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so these letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: something that came about has happened
taken as written
ill can mean bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: Someone discovered in bed turns out to have a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a sickbed, and 'to have' only joins the past tense to the reversed part.
explanation.definitionFit: A camellia is a flowering shrub grown in garden borders, so it is one thing a gardener plants there.

clue.text: American playwright discussed on the beach?

indicators.note: something discussed is talked about, so we hear the word spoken rather than see it written

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
George Bernard Shaw, the playwright, said in a non-rhotic British accent

explanation.surface: A US dramatist being talked about while relaxing by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American playwright' suggests one name, but only A is American; Shaw was Irish. In British speech SHAW and SHORE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ashore means being on land at the coast, which a beach is; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Perhaps Bering, Blixen and Kierkegaard, or certain 7s?

blocks.note: first meaning: eminent people from Denmark, the explorer Vitus Bering, the author Karen Blixen and the philosopher
second meaning: a large breed of dog, and dogs are what 7-down is

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 7-down, BARKER, a word for a dog. All three named people were famous Danes.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous Danish figures are literally distinguished Danes, and the giant dog breed carries the same name.

clue.text: Crew member checks mounting fear in two ways

indicators.note: in a down entry something mounting climbs upward, so its letters run bottom to top
one thing sitting in others is placed inside them

blocks.note: awe is reverential fear
ST for street and RD for road, two abbreviations for ways

explanation.surface: A crew member checks someone's growing panic in two different manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two ways' sounds like 'in two manners', but the ways are a street and a road, split around the fear. 'Checks' just links, as a steward checks passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is a cabin attendant on a ship or aircraft, so one of its crew.

clue.text: Son, mine, an exact likeness

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A parent remarks that their boy is their exact double.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as the possessive in 'my son', but it is the noun: a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom 'the spit of' or 'spitting image', meaning someone who closely resembles another person.

clue.text: Car capital leaves nothing — just endless rubble

indicators.note: when something leaves it departs, so a letter is dropped from the word
having no ends means both the first and final letters go, keeping only the inside

blocks.note: Detroit, Michigan, is the historic centre of the US motor industry
O looks like zero, nothing
the inner letters of the word

explanation.surface: Motor City has emptied out, leaving only rubble behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Detroit without its O gives DETRIT, then the middle of JUST adds US. The surface fits Detroit's industrial decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is loose debris or waste fragments, a close synonym for broken rubble.

clue.text: One earning crust from bread engages right tout

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a baker earns a living, a crust, by making bread
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bread seller takes on a shady ticket seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earning a crust' is British slang for making a living, punning on a baker's bread crust.
explanation.definitionFit: A barker is a person outside a fairground show shouting to attract customers, which is what a tout does.

clue.text: Language without appeal draws in two kings

indicators.note: drawing something in pulls it inside, so other letters are enclosed

blocks.note: sans is French for without, used in English
it means sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'
K is king in chess notation; R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A dull language somehow still attracts two monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without appeal' is read as two words and the kings go between them. 'It' for sex appeal is an old convention, as in the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient classical tongue of India, used in Hindu scripture.

clue.text: Building quickly assembled before cracking

blocks.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
cracking and fab are both British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A hastily put-up building that started to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like structural failure but is British slang for excellent, as is FAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house made from factory-built sections and put up on site in days.

clue.text: Obstacle on marshland where ship departs

indicators.note: a vessel that departs is no longer there, so its abbreviation is removed

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
a morass is a bog
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A hazard on a boggy coast at the point where a vessel leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a rare sense: Latin remora means delay, and the sucker fish got its name from supposedly holding ships back.
explanation.definitionFit: Remora is an old word for a hindrance, from the fish believed to slow down ships by clinging to them.

clue.text: Engage in sport and kit wears out

indicators.note: something gone out of order is disordered, so the letters are put back in a different sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Playing games regularly means your sports gear gets worn through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wears out' reads as one phrasal verb; split it, and the final word is the signal while the two before it are the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To waterski is to take part in a water sport, towed behind a motorboat on skis.

clue.text: Enemy circles large ice sheet

indicators.note: to circle something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a foe is an enemy
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A foe prowls around a vast expanse of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' looks like a description of the ice sheet, but it supplies the L inside FOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a flat mass of floating sea ice, one kind of ice sheet.

clue.text: Offensive revolutionary deeply hurt a right-winger

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so these letters are read backwards

blocks.note: gored means pierced by a horn
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A radical attacks a conservative politician in a nasty way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun, the radical doing the hurting, but it turns GORED round. Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks are disparaging or insulting, so offensive in the sense of giving offence.

clue.text: Warmer in the main with huge opening flower?

blocks.note: a gulf is a vast chasm or gap
a stream is something that flows, a 'flow-er'

explanation.surface: A tropical bloom opening wide in mostly warm weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the classic crossword trick: something that flows, not a bloom. 'The main' is the sea, not 'mainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf Stream is the warm Atlantic current that heats western Europe, an ocean current that warms.

clue.text: Short holiday viewed as sound, healthy preparation?

indicators.note: taken as sound means heard rather than read, so a word that is pronounced the same is wanted

blocks.note: vac is short for vacation
the film prefix cine is said like seen

explanation.surface: A short break judged to be a sound way of getting fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' and 'healthy' look like a pair of adjectives; 'as sound' instead turns 'viewed' into its spoken twin.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccine is a medical preparation that protects against disease, keeping a person healthy.

clue.text: Peevish with formal greeting showing arm

blocks.note: cross means irritable
a bow is a formal way to greet someone

explanation.surface: Someone grumpy greeting another stiffly while holding out a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' suggests a limb; it means a weapon, as in firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow for shooting bolts, so a weapon, which is one sense of arm.

clue.text: Storm in Belgium with freakish result

indicators.note: something freakish is abnormal and distorted, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A storm hits Belgium and has strange consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' reads as a noun for the weather, but it is the verb: to rant.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluster is to talk loudly and aggressively, just as to storm is to rage or rant.

clue.text: Weird Scots rook inside the Spanish moat?

indicators.note: a thing inside another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
a moat is one kind of ditch, hence the question mark
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A strange Scottish chess piece hides within a Spanish castle's moat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' looks like the people around the rook, but it marks the definition as a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldritch is a Scottish word for uncanny or eerie, so it is the Scots term for strange.

clue.text: Some terrible mishap brings scar

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters come from a portion of the phrase

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the next

explanation.surface: A bad accident leaves a lasting mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across terriBLE MISHap.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a mark that spoils a surface, and a scar is one such mark on the skin.

clue.text: Purgative from sailors in Surrey?

blocks.note: Epsom is a town in the county of Surrey, south of London
old salts are seasoned sailors

explanation.surface: A laxative obtained from seamen based in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county just south of London; the question mark warns that Epsom is just one example of a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts, magnesium sulphate, are taken by mouth as a laxative, which is a purgative.

clue.text: Swimmer one put outside

indicators.note: one thing outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to place is to put

explanation.surface: A swimmer is told to get out of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put outside' looks like an instruction to eject someone; it is PLACE wrapped around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaice is a flatfish, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Woman into bed with Democrat

indicators.note: going into something means being put inside it

blocks.note: to lay is slang for to bed someone
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A woman climbs into bed beside a Democrat politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Democrat goes into the verb for bedding someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a polite word for a woman, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Ulster manoeuvring shows brilliance

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things around into new positions, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland's political deft footwork is praised as brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster, the province of Northern Ireland, is simply the six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a gleaming sheen or glory, so brilliance in either the shining or the splendid sense.

clue.text: Music rocks on beat that can be hot

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: something that can be hot

indicators.note: rocking shakes things about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to cap is to outdo or beat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hot rock music with a pounding beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music rocks' and 'beat' sound like a gig review; 'rocks' jumbles MUSIC and 'beat' gives CAP, which goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the pepper genus, including chillies, whose fruits range from mild to fiercely spicy.

clue.text: Characters inside school getting cooked salmon

indicators.note: the letters lying inside a word are its interior, with the ends discarded
cooking changes ingredients into something different, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the inner letters of the word, without its first and last

explanation.surface: Pupils at a school are served cooked salmon for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests a school of fish to go with the salmon, but only its middle letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The coho is a Pacific salmon species, also called silver salmon.

clue.text: Country game needs good man in charge

blocks.note: RU stands for rugby union
ST, saint, is a good man
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A national team's match requires a decent person running it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a nation; it is the adjective, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic describes things of the countryside, simple rural life and style, so it means country as an adjective.

clue.text: Jack meets fool and hospital cleaner

blocks.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
clot is British slang for an idiot
H is the map sign for hospital

explanation.surface: A man called Jack runs into an idiot and a hospital cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hospital cleaner' reads as a job title; the cleaner stands alone as the definition. A J-cloth is a British brand of disposable cleaning cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A J-cloth is a thin household wiping cloth, so a cleaning item used for wiping down surfaces.

clue.text: Is it paste produced in this plant?

blocks.clueFragment: Is it paste produced in this plant?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about whether a factory makes glue or paste
setter's reading: paste is imitation jewellery, so a fake gem, and the plant's name splits into fake plus gem

explanation.surface: Someone touring a factory asks whether glue is made here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory and 'paste' like glue, but paste is fake jewellery: a sham rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock is a clover-like three-leaved plant, the national emblem of Ireland.
